repo_notes.content:
WHAT THIS PROJECT IS. MiSTer Linux Modernization (this repository, `Buildroot_MiSTer`) is a Buildroot BR2_EXTERNAL tree (external name `MISTER`, declared in `external.desc`; paths inside the tree are written `$(BR2_EXTERNAL_MISTER_PATH)/...`) that builds the Linux operating system a MiSTer runs on the ARM side of a Terasic DE10-Nano. Its outputs are: a mainline kernel.org LTS kernel with every MiSTer kernel change carried as an ordered series of `.patch` files against the pristine, hash-verified tarball; a Buildroot ext4 root filesystem image (`linux.img`); the concatenated kernel plus device tree that U-Boot boots (`zImage_dtb`); a second, PREEMPT_RT kernel (`zImage_dtb-rt`) whose modules live in the same `linux.img`; a flashable SD-card image with a first-boot installer (`sdcard.img.xz`); the release archive (`release_YYYYMMDD.7z`) and the `db.json` that the stock on-device Downloader reads; and the CI that builds, checks and publishes all of it. The same tree also builds a bare developer OS for the Terasic DE25-Nano (Agilex 5, aarch64) from its own defconfig.

It is a drop-in replacement for stock's Linux image. The unmodified stock `MiSTer` binary (Main_MiSTer) and existing cores run on it unchanged; this repository never builds or modifies that binary, the cores or the menu core. It replaces files under `/media/fat/linux/` and installs a few launchers under `/media/fat/Scripts/`. The README's stated posture is "prove parity first, then improve": match stock's behaviour (not only its file list), carry the smallest kernel delta, make builds reproducible, never commit binaries, and distribute opt-in through the stock Downloader. Describe it as an OS image plus its build, test and release machinery: not a fork of Main_MiSTer, not a core, not a channel for cores.

SCOPE AND STATUS TO KEEP ON EVERY PAGE. The README status line is binding: "personal use only"; validated on one real DE10-Nano; nothing is offered publicly until a named maintainer signs the sustainability commitment in ADR 0014 (`docs/decisions/0014-sustainability-deferred-not-waived.md`); contributions open once the Phase 4 publication gate is passed. Take what has and has not been verified on hardware only from the README sections "What has been verified, and what has not" and "Hardware validation ledger" (evidence in `docs/testlogs/`). Anything not listed there is unverified. Most Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chips, Samba and MIDI are build/CI-verified only; RT latency has not been measured; mainline U-Boot builds but ships nowhere; the DE25-Nano has not run on hardware. Never upgrade "builds", "QEMU-tested" or "CI-verified" to "works" or "supported", never call a packaged-but-not-enabled package part of the image, and never present the project as official MiSTer software or as endorsed by the MiSTer FPGA project.

AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES, in this order.

1. The build inputs. `Makefile` (the Buildroot pin and the few wrapper targets), `configs/mister_de10nano_defconfig` and `configs/mister_de25nano_defconfig` (every board option and pin), the top-level `Config.in` and `external.mk`, each `package/<name>/` (`Config.in`, `<name>.mk`, `<name>.hash`, patches), `board/mister/*/` and `linux/`. For what the build does, these files win over any prose; when a document disagrees with them, say so and cite both.
2. `README.md`: what the project is, its status and hardware ledger, the install command and what it changes, the release asset set, the build quick start, and the documentation map. It is the source of record for status wording.
3. The ADRs in `docs/decisions/` for why things are the way they are. Read each ADR's Status line and report it as written: some are Proposed, one is Deferred, one is "accepted in direction", one is "provisionally accepted", and several carry dated amendments or are superseded in part by a later ADR.
4. The topic documents in `docs/`. Contracts: `docs/abi-contract.md`, `docs/boot-chain.md`, `docs/downloader-contract.md`. Engineering: `docs/buildroot-config.md`, `docs/ci.md`, `docs/renovate.md`, `docs/reproducibility.md`, `docs/rt-beta-kernel.md`, `docs/kernel-export.md`, `docs/patch-provenance.md`, `docs/kernel-config-deltas.md`, `docs/installer-init.md`, `docs/installer-build.md`, `docs/minijail.md`. Parity audits: `docs/*-parity.md`, `docs/stock-reconciliation.md`, `docs/stock-binary-reconciliation.md`, `docs/version-delta.md`. DE25: `docs/de25-nano-overview.md` and the other `docs/de25-*.md`. User procedures: `docs/user/`.
5. The header comment blocks of scripts and workflows: `install.sh`, `uninstall.sh`, `board/mister/de10nano/fat-payload/Scripts/*.sh`, `scripts/*.sh` and `scripts/*.py`, `board/mister/common/initramfs-overlay/init`, the installer, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/actions/*/action.yml` and `.github/actions/README.md`. They say what each file does and why, and many are more current than the docs.
6. `PLAN.md` and `TASKS.md`: the original plan, the constraint index (A1 to A15, `TASKS.md` section A) and the phase task IDs (P0.x to P5.x). Cite them for history and for constraint IDs, not for current state.
7. `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `LICENSE` and the README "Contributing and licensing" section.

VERSIONS AND NUMBERS: NO DRIFTING METRICS. Do not write patch counts, package counts, the number of workflows or ADRs, free-space or size percentages, measured image sizes, per-package versions, or "tested on kernel X.Y.Z". These change weekly through Renovate. Say where the value lives instead: the Buildroot pin is `BUILDROOT_VERSION` (with `BUILDROOT_SHA256`) in `Makefile`; the kernel pins are `BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CUSTOM_VERSION_VALUE` in each defconfig and `BR2_PACKAGE_LINUX_RT_VERSION` in `configs/mister_de10nano_defconfig`, with hashes in `board/mister/de10nano/patches/linux/linux.hash`, `package/linux-rt/linux-rt.hash` and `board/mister/de25nano/patches/linux/linux.hash`; package versions are in Buildroot's own `.mk` files at the pinned release or this tree's `package/<name>/<name>.mk`; each release's `legal-info` is the authoritative list. You may name a kernel line the way the docs do (the LTS line of the main kernel, the 7.x line the RT variant tracks), but take it from the pins. Many documents open with a dated warning that they were measured against an older stock release or older package versions; keep that caveat whenever you use them, and do not restate their figures as current. Comments next to a pin can lag the pin (a header naming an older line, or a file that no longer exists); always prefer the value line.

DIRECTORIES THAT MATTER, most important first.

- `configs/`: the two committed defconfigs, in Buildroot's own `savedefconfig` form.
- `package/`: this tree's Buildroot packages, grouped into menus by the top-level `Config.in`. Three are Kconfig profiles with no build of their own (`package/mister-userspace`, `package/mister-firmware`, `package/mister-drivers`): each `select`s a documented package set. `package/linux-rt` is the second kernel. `package/mister-initramfs`, `package/mister-initramfs-busybox` and `package/mister-initramfs-exfatprogs` build the stage-1 cpio. The rest are out-of-tree drivers, firmware, libraries and tools.
- `linux/` (`linux/Config.ext.in`, `linux/linux-ext-mister-initramfs.mk`): a Buildroot linux extension that makes the stage-1 cpio a kernel dependency and points `CONFIG_INITRAMFS_SOURCE` at it.
- `board/mister/de10nano/`: `linux.config` (minimal kernel defconfig), `linux-rt.fragment` (the RT delta), `linux-patches/` (the series Buildroot applies to the main kernel), `linux-patches-beta/` (the RT kernel's series: a `series` file listing symlinks into `linux-patches/` plus re-anchored copies and beta-only patches, reached through the `patches/linux-rt` symlink), `linux-patches-upstream/` (applied only by the export script, never to the image), `patches/<package>/` (BR2_GLOBAL_PATCH_DIR: per-package patches and hash files, including U-Boot's), `rootfs-overlay/`, `post-build.sh`, `post-image.sh`, `users.table`, `busybox.fragment`, `uboot.fragment`, `uboot.env`, `genimage-sdcard.cfg`, `initramfs-overlay/` (the first-boot installer), `installer-splash/` and `fsck-splash/` (splash images with their build scripts), and `fat-payload/` (files that go onto the FAT card: the Scripts-menu launchers, `downloader.ini`, `linux/security.conf`).
- `board/mister/common/`: board-neutral pieces: the stage-1 `/init` (`board/mister/common/initramfs-overlay/init`), the installer-flag probe and its definition (`usr/lib/mister/install-flag`, `install-flag.conf`), the initramfs BusyBox config, and `linux-mister.fragment` (the arch-neutral MiSTer kernel personality the DE25 kernel config layers on).
- `board/mister/de25nano/`: the DE25 kernel config, device tree, U-Boot device tree, patches, genimage config and post-image script.
- `scripts/`: the test suite (`scripts/ci-tests.sh`, `scripts/test-*.sh`, `scripts/check-*.sh`), release and card builders (`scripts/mk-release.sh`, `scripts/mk-sdcard.sh`, `scripts/fetch-sdcard-payload.sh`, `scripts/verify-stock-payload.sh`), db.json tooling (`scripts/gen-db-json.py`, `scripts/check-db-json-schema.py`, `scripts/db_entity_contract.py`), hash sync (`scripts/hash-sync-*.sh`, `scripts/lib/hash-sync-common.sh`), kernel export and fork tracking (`scripts/export-kernel-tree.sh`, `scripts/check-export-tree.sh`, `scripts/check-fork-sync.sh`), the Buildroot fetcher (`scripts/fetch-buildroot.sh`, `scripts/hostshim.sh`), and stock-inventory tooling (`scripts/inventory/`).
- `.github/`: workflows, the composite actions `buildroot-build` and `verify-image`, issue templates, `actionlint.yaml`. `renovate.json` at the root.
- `install.sh`, `uninstall.sh`: run on the MiSTer itself.

NOT SOURCE TO DOCUMENT AS CODE.
- `work/` (the fetched Buildroot tree, the host shim), `output*/`, `dl/`, `dist/`: build output and download cache, ignored by git. Never describe their contents as part of the repository.
- `docs/stock-inventory/<release>/`, the `.txt`, `.diff` and `.tsv` files under `docs/verification/`, `docs/kernel-recon/records/`, `docs/kernel-recon/reconciliation.jsonl` and `docs/kernel-recon/fork-sync-2026-09/`: recorded evidence and generated tables about stock and the upstream kernel fork. Cite them as evidence; do not summarise them row by row or turn their counts into claims.
- `docs/testlogs/`: hardware logs, the evidence behind the README ledger.
- `docs/dwc2-usb-irq/lab/` and `docs/dwc2-usb-irq/parked/`: research tools and parked patches the build does not apply.
- `art/` and `art-src/`: the Root Kun mascot artwork and its generator. Mention them in the overview only; their licence is not GPLv3 (README).
- `MISTER-KERNEL-PATCH-RECON.md`: an archived spec kept for its method; it is not the live process.
- Generated, not in the tree: `db.json` (made by `scripts/gen-db-json.py` in `publish-db.yml` and served from GitHub Pages), the release assets, the exported Linux-Kernel_MiSTer-style git tree and its `EXPORT.md`.

VOCABULARY. Use these terms as the tree does.

- stock: the official MiSTer Linux image. "Release YYYYMMDD" names a stock release; the docs pin and compare against specific ones.
- the `MiSTer` binary, Main_MiSTer: the stock main program. This repository consumes it (for ABI tests and in the release archive's stock tree) and never builds it.
- the Downloader (`Downloader_MiSTer`), Update All (`update_all.sh`), `Scripts/update.sh`: the stock on-device updaters. Update All runs the Downloader with the same `/media/fat/downloader.ini`.
- `db.json`: a Downloader database. This project's has `db_id` `mister_linux_modernization` and a `linux` entry describing `release_YYYYMMDD.7z` (schema in `scripts/gen-db-json.py` and `docs/downloader-contract.md` section 1).
- `/MiSTer.version`: the stamp at the rootfs root that the Downloader compares by inequality; set in `board/mister/de10nano/post-build.sh` and derived from the release date (ADR 0018).
- `linux.img`: the ext4 root filesystem image, a file on the FAT card at `/media/fat/linux/linux.img`, loop-mounted read-only.
- `zImage_dtb`, `zImage_dtb-rt`: zImage and DTB concatenated byte-exactly by `board/mister/de10nano/post-image.sh` and checked by `scripts/check-zimage-dtb.sh`.
- stage 1, the stage-1 initramfs, `mister-initramfs.cpio`: the BusyBox cpio embedded in each DE10 kernel. Its `/init` replaces stock's `loop=` kernel patch (ADR 0002) and also hosts the first-boot installer (ADR 0033) and the exFAT repair (ADR 0026).
- `/media/fat`: the data partition (exFAT, or FAT32), mounted `sync,dirsync`.
- the 0xA2 partition, `uboot.img`: the raw bootloader partition and stock's U-Boot image, which this project ships byte-identical, fetched by hash.
- the installer flag: MBR entry 3 of type 0xda plus a magic block at LBA 1024 (`board/mister/common/initramfs-overlay/usr/lib/mister/install-flag.conf`). It is what makes a card install instead of boot.
- profiles: `BR2_PACKAGE_MISTER_USERSPACE`, `BR2_PACKAGE_MISTER_FIRMWARE`, `BR2_PACKAGE_MISTER_DRIVERS`.
- beta, the 7.x series: the RT kernel's line and its patch directory `linux-patches-beta/`. In file names "beta" means that kernel line, not a release channel.
- the kill switch: `[MiSTer] update_linux = false` in `downloader.ini` (ADR 0025). The private updater: `Scripts/update_linux_modernization.sh`.
- `.mlm-backup`: `/media/fat/linux/.mlm-backup/`, where `install.sh` saves the files it replaces.
- the security state file: `/media/fat/linux/security.conf` (template `board/mister/de10nano/fat-payload/linux/security.conf`). A missing key or file means stock behaviour.
- ADRs: `docs/decisions/NNNN-*.md`. The numbering has gaps, and two different ADRs are numbered 0025 (first-boot timezone autodetect; the update_linux kill switch). Always cite an ADR with its file name, and never invent the missing numbers.
- Task IDs: P0.x to P5.x (`TASKS.md`), the D-series DE25 tasks (`docs/de25-nano-tasks.md`), constraints A1 to A15 (`TASKS.md` section A).
- the test board, the rig: the one DE10-Nano everything hardware-verified ran on.

LAYOUT HISTORY: DO NOT DESCRIBE REMOVED MECHANISMS AS CURRENT. Several documents were written before the tree was reshaped, and many keep their old text under a dated note.

- ADR 0030 (`docs/decisions/0030-makefile-toward-vanilla-buildroot.md`) shrank the wrapper `Makefile` to a thin forwarder, replaced the Buildroot-config fragment stacks (`configs/fragments/`, `mister_kernel_defconfig`, `mister_rt.fragment`, the `output-rt/` tree, the kernel-variant matrix) with two committed defconfigs and the Kconfig profile packages, and turned the RT kernel into `package/linux-rt` inside the one build. `docs/buildroot-config.md` still holds the per-line rationale; its "Layout change" box maps old sections to where those lines live now, and marks its sections 1, 7, 8 and 11 as historical. `docs/ci.md` has a "Historical design notes (pre-ADR 0030)" part. Some file headers (for example in `board/mister/de10nano/linux-rt.fragment`) still name files from before this change.
- ADR 0033 (`docs/decisions/0033-one-initramfs-installer-in-stage-1.md`) moved the SD-card installer into the one stage-1 cpio. `mister_installer_defconfig` and the `output-installer/` tree are gone, and `make sdcard` is pure assembly of `make`'s outputs. ADR 0033's status is Proposed: built and QEMU-tested.
- ADR 0024 superseded part of ADR 0017: a mainline U-Boot is built as a capability artifact, but the card still ships stock's `uboot.img`.
- ADR 0019 amended ADR 0010 (exFAT symlinks). ADR 0025 (kill switch) replaced the "win the multi-db race by keeping db.json small" approach. ADR 0026 was amended by ADR 0033.
- Stock moved its own kernel during this project (`docs/verification/stock-release-*.md`). The kernel reconciliation therefore separates the original stock baseline from upstream's newer branch; read `docs/kernel-recon/reconciliation.md` "How to read this table" before describing either.

Describe the tree as it is now. Mention a removed file or mechanism only as history, and label it as history.

WRITING RULES.

- Quote paths, Kconfig symbols, make targets, script options, environment variables and workflow names exactly as they appear. Never invent a file, symbol, target, option, workflow, ADR, issue or figure. If you cannot confirm something, name the file that would settle it.
- When sources disagree (the README and a dated document header; a workflow's `on:` block and a table in the README or `docs/ci.md`; a comment and the value line beneath it), report both and say which file is binding. The files themselves win for behaviour; the README wins for status.
- Keep safety warnings. The first-boot installer's header says it can brick the board; the DE25 U-Boot build fails if any QSPI-write path is enabled; the Downloader's `updateboot` rewrites the bootloader and wipes the saved U-Boot environment. State these plainly.
- Stay inside this repository. Describe other projects (Main_MiSTer, Downloader_MiSTer, Update_All_MiSTer, Linux-Kernel_MiSTer, ItsAlive_MiSTer, Menu_MiSTer and other upstreams) only as far as this tree's packages, pins and documents describe them, and do not guess at their internals or plans. Some patch headers and documents name particular out-of-tree userspace programs as prospective users of a kernel interface; describe such an interface as available to any userspace client, and do not name or speculate about those programs.
- Do not narrate how documents were produced (tooling, agent runs, model names, spend limits). Dates, task IDs and ADR numbers are fine. Do not write GitHub user handles; say "the maintainer". Include no personal details.
- Upstreaming: say only what `docs/patch-provenance.md`, `docs/kernel-export.md` and the patch headers record about what was sent to or accepted by Linux-Kernel_MiSTer.
- Prefer short tables and command blocks taken from the source over paraphrase. Give a user command exactly as the README or `docs/user/` gives it.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Introduce MiSTer Linux Modernization: what it builds (kernel, root filesystem, RT kernel variant, SD-card image, release archive and db.json), for which board, and why it exists (stock's userland comes from an old Buildroot with no public build recipe, its kernel is pinned to one point release, and there is no SBOM, CI or update path). Give the parity-first posture, the drop-in-replacement promise and its one stated requirement on the Main_MiSTer release, the status line, and a map of the rest of the wiki. End with the licensing split and a short note on the Root Kun mascot.

page_notes.content:
Sources: README.md (the opening paragraphs, "Why this exists", the status quote block, "How it is put together", "Contributing and licensing", "Meet Root Kun"), `external.desc`, `PLAN.md` sections 1 and 2.

Lead with the status line exactly as the README words it ("personal use only", validated on one real DE10-Nano, ADR 0014 sustainability gate) and link `docs/user/beta-testing.md`. Quote the minimum Main_MiSTer release from the README and its reason; do not restate it from memory.

Give the "How it is put together" tree as a table of top-level directories, using the repo notes' directory list. Explain the kernel model in one sentence: there is no separate kernel repository; the kernel is the pinned kernel.org tarball plus an ordered patch series. The DE25-Nano is a second, bare developer OS built from the same tree with no MiSTer binaries; link its page.

Licensing (README): repository code GPLv3 (`LICENSE`); kernel patches under `board/mister/*/linux-patches*/` GPLv2; packages under their upstream licences, with each release's `legal-info` as the SBOM; the MiSTer Kun artwork (`art/`, `art-src/upstream/`, `board/mister/de10nano/installer-splash/`) is by its credited authors under its own terms (`board/mister/de10nano/installer-splash/upstream/LICENSE`) and is not GPLv3.

Do not copy the README's version-comparison table numbers into this page; link the "Compared With Stock MiSTer" page instead.

pages.title: Status, Scope and Hardware Validation
pages.purpose: Set out precisely what has been verified and how: the phase table (0 to 5) and its state, the hardware validation ledger row by row, what is build- or CI-verified only, the known limitations (including the one known regression, the temporary debug tooling and the open sustainability gate), and what "personal use only" and "beta" mean for someone deciding whether to run it.

page_notes.content:
Sources: README "What has been verified, and what has not", "Hardware validation ledger" and "Known limitations"; `docs/user/beta-testing.md`; `docs/testlogs/` (`p1-first-boot.md`, `p2-menu.md`, `p3-matrix.md` and the dated logs); `docs/decisions/0014-sustainability-deferred-not-waived.md`; `docs/debug-tooling.md`; `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/hardware_report.yml` and `bug_report.yml`.

Reproduce the ledger's rows and status symbols as written. Do not add rows, and do not merge "build-verified" into "verified". Where a topic document has its own dated status table, show it beside the ledger instead of choosing one: `docs/rt-beta-kernel.md` section 6 records which RT kernel pins have booted on the board and that the currently pinned line has been built and QEMU-tested but not booted, and that latency is unproven; `docs/dwc2-usb-irq.md` gives its own verification state; the DE25 documents state that no hardware has been touched.

Explain the sustainability gate from ADR 0014 (deferred, not waived; what a maintainer would commit to) and that contributions open after the Phase 4 gate (README, `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

For known limitations, take each item from the README and link its source document (the G923 PlayStation variant in `docs/patch-provenance.md` section 9; the forward-ported cpufreq lesson; debug tooling in `docs/debug-tooling.md`, designed to revert as one unit; package versions not asserted by CI). End with how to report a problem: the issue templates and `docs/user/beta-testing.md` "What to report".

pages.title: Compared With Stock MiSTer
pages.purpose: Explain how this image relates to stock: what is deliberately identical (the MiSTer binary's ABI and SONAMEs, the boot chain and uboot.img, /media/fat mount flags, the read-only root with its login-time remount, exFAT with symlinks, the Bluetooth key store, RTC, MIDI/MT-32, Samba, SSH/FTP, BusyBox applets and init scripts, /MiSTer.version and the Downloader contract), what is different and why, and how parity is established and audited (stock inventories, per-subsystem parity audits, the stock binary reconciliation). Guide the reader to the right audit for each subsystem.

page_notes.content:
Sources: README "Stock vs. this image", "Deliberately identical to stock" and the parity-audit line in "Documentation map"; `docs/stock-reconciliation.md`; `docs/stock-binary-reconciliation.md` (with `docs/stock-inventory/20260907/binary-recon/`); `docs/version-delta.md`; `docs/stock-inventory/README.md`; `docs/verification/stock-release-20250402.md`, `docs/verification/stock-release-20260907.md`, `docs/verification/stock-release-20260912.md`; the audits `docs/init-parity.md`, `docs/wifi-parity.md`, `docs/bluetooth-parity.md`, `docs/firmware-parity.md`, `docs/usb-automount-parity.md`, `docs/netfs-parity.md`, `docs/samba-parity.md`, `docs/ssh-ftp-parity.md`, `docs/midi-mt32-parity.md`, `docs/rtc-parity.md`, `docs/util-linux-parity.md`; `docs/package-manifest.md`.

Present the comparison as categories (kernel source and update policy, userland base, TLS library, network-facing software, SSH host keys and key login, remote root login, the `.7z` extractor, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth coverage, filesystems, timezone, image headroom, build recipe, reproducibility/SBOM, dependency updates, RT kernel, fresh-card install) and say which file holds each fact. Do not copy version numbers or percentages from the README table into prose: they are dated readings, and the README says the build pins are the ground truth. If you show the table, say it is the README's reading on its stated date.

Every parity audit carries a dated header; several say they were measured against an older stock release or an older package version. Keep that caveat next to anything you take from them. `docs/stock-inventory/` holds data extracted from stock releases; describe what kind of data it is and how `scripts/inventory/` regenerates it (`scripts/inventory/README.md`), not its contents.

pages.title: Installing and Updating
pages.purpose: Give the user-facing picture of getting this image onto a MiSTer and keeping it current: the three ways in (the one-command converter on an existing card, a fresh card from sdcard.img.xz, the by-hand procedure), how updates arrive afterwards through a private Downloader run, how to roll back, and which document in docs/user/ to read for each situation. Keep the personal-use status visible.

page_notes.content:
Sources: README "Install it on a real MiSTer" and "Updates and the release channel"; `docs/user/README.md` (the table of user documents and when to read each); `docs/user/onboarding.md`; `docs/user/sdcard-flashing.md`; `docs/user/rollback.md`; `docs/user/faq.md`.

This is a landing page. Keep each route to a paragraph and link its child page. Give the install one-liner exactly as the README prints it, with the README's warning that on a stock card it fails silently because stock curl cannot verify GitHub, and the README's `-k` download-then-run form. Say that the installer prints what it will change and counts down before acting, and that `--dry-run` changes nothing.

State the trust model as the README does: piping a remote script to a root shell is the same HTTPS-to-GitHub trust model as MiSTer's own `update.sh`, and the download-and-read and by-hand routes exist for anyone who does not want that.

pages.title: Converting a Card, Rolling Back and Recovery
pages.purpose: Document converting an existing MiSTer card with install.sh: its preconditions, the CA-bundle check and --bootstrap-ca, every file it replaces or installs and what it leaves alone, the backups it takes, the side effects any Linux update has (the U-Boot environment wipe, a one-time SSH host-key change), and its options. Then document leaving: update_linux_modernization.sh --restore-stock, uninstall.sh and its options, the by-hand rollback, and serial-console recovery when a board does not boot.

page_notes.content:
Sources: `install.sh` (the "WHAT IT DOES" header, the option parser and usage line, `BACKUP_FILES`, `install_scripts`), README "Install it on a real MiSTer" (the "What it changes" and "What it leaves alone" tables), `uninstall.sh` (its header and option parser), `board/mister/de10nano/fat-payload/Scripts/update_linux_modernization.sh` (`--restore-stock`, `--status`), `docs/user/onboarding.md`, `docs/user/rollback.md`, `docs/user/serial-recovery.md`, `docs/user/faq.md` (host-key and update questions), ADR 0025 (`docs/decisions/0025-update-linux-kill-switch-and-private-updater.md`), ADR 0015 (`docs/decisions/0015-per-device-ssh-host-keys.md`).

Facts to get right: `install.sh` options are `--dry-run`, `--yes`/`-y`, `--no-reboot` and `--bootstrap-ca`; confirm against its usage line. `uninstall.sh` options are `--no-flash`, `--remove-script` and `--restore-backups`; describe each from its header. The installer writes `[MiSTer] update_linux = false` into `downloader.ini` and saves the original under `linux/.mlm-backup/`. It installs the Scripts launchers named in `install_scripts` (check the list there: `sinden_lightgun.sh` exists in `fat-payload/` but is not in that list). Network identity files are copied into the new image before it goes live. pages.title: Updates, db.json and the Downloader Contract
pages.purpose: Explain how updates reach a converted card and why it is built this way: the Downloader applies at most one Linux image per run and the official database wins, so the image uses the update_linux kill switch plus a private updater that runs the Downloader against a private ini naming only this project's database. Sources: `docs/downloader-contract.md` (sections 1 to 13; it is line-cited against a pinned Downloader_MiSTer commit, so take Downloader behaviour from it and say so), `docs/db-json-versioning.md`, ADR 0018 (`docs/decisions/0018-db-json-version-is-release-date-driven.md`), ADR 0025 (`docs/decisions/0025-update-linux-kill-switch-and-private-updater.md`), ADR 0012 (`docs/decisions/0012-multi-db-defer-test-by-sd-copy.md`), `board/mister/de10nano/fat-payload/Scripts/update_linux_modernization.sh` (its "WHY THIS SCRIPT EXISTS" header and options `--status`, `--force`, `--no-reboot`, `--setup-only`, `--restore-stock`), `board/mister/de10nano/fat-payload/downloader.ini`, `scripts/gen-db-json.py` (the schema block in its docstring), `scripts/check-db-json-schema.py`, `scripts/db_entity_contract.py`, `.github/workflows/publish-db.yml`, `board/mister/de10nano/post-build.sh` (the `/MiSTer.version` block), `scripts/mk-release.sh` step 1.

Walk the apply flow in `docs/downloader-contract.md` section 7 order. Explain the multi-database rule from section 9 and ADR 0025's Context, then the chosen design: no daemon, no boot script, one deliberate user action. State why the version stamp is derived from the release date: the Downloader compares by inequality, and reproducible builds pin `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.

On generation: `publish-db.yml` runs on a published release (or a manual dispatch naming a tag, deliberately with no "latest" default), generates `db.json` with `scripts/gen-db-json.py`, checks it again with `scripts/check-db-json-schema.py`, and deploys it to GitHub Pages. Show the db.json `linux` schema from `gen-db-json.py`'s docstring rather than writing one from memory.

pages.title: SD-Card Image and First-Boot Installer

Sources: ADR 0020 (`docs/decisions/0020-sdcard-exfat-reformat-installer.md`), ADR 0033 (`docs/decisions/0033-one-initramfs-installer-in-stage-1.md`), ADR 0017 (`docs/decisions/0017-uboot-from-mister-fork-full-sd-image.md`), `docs/installer-init.md` (the flag, the ten steps, recoverability, load-bearing facts, splash, commit phase, test hook, rescue), `docs/installer-build.md`, `board/mister/de10nano/initramfs-overlay/usr/libexec/mister-installer/install` (its tunables block), `board/mister/common/initramfs-overlay/usr/lib/mister/install-flag` and `install-flag.conf`, `board/mister/de10nano/genimage-sdcard.cfg`, `scripts/mk-sdcard.sh`, `scripts/fetch-sdcard-payload.sh`, `docs/verification/sdcard-payload.md`, `board/mister/de10nano/installer-splash/README.md`, `package/itsalive/Config.in`, `docs/user/sdcard-flashing.md`, and the tests `scripts/test-installer-mbr.sh`, `scripts/test-installer-recovery.sh`, `scripts/test-installer-splash.sh`, `scripts/test-sdcard-install.sh`.

Facts to get right. Linux cannot grow exFAT in place, which is why the card is reformatted rather than grown. Take install-time behaviour, RAM reserve, trim and recovery behaviour from the installer and `docs/installer-init.md`, not from memory.

`make sdcard` (`SDCARD_CORES=1` for the full variant) is pure assembly after `make`. `fetch-sdcard-payload.sh` stages the pinned stock release archive (the source of the byte-identical `uboot.img`, verified after extraction), the pinned launchers (Update All, `wifi.sh`), this project's `fat-payload/` files and, for the full variant only, a pinned `_Console` cores snapshot; read the exact list from the script. A card flashed from this image starts with the hardened security state (see the security page). Card contents such as which core databases are enabled come from `fat-payload/downloader.ini`; quote it.

itsalive lights HDMI without Main_MiSTer so a first-time user sees "do not power off"; it ships only in the DE10 stage-1 cpio and must never run while Main_MiSTer is up (`package/itsalive/Config.in`). Describe it only as that file and `package/itsalive/itsalive.mk` do; its source lives in a separate repository.

Facts to get right. `check_storage.sh` runs a read-only scan, and a repair happens only after confirmation, on the next boot, from stage 1 (ADR 0026, as amended by ADR 0033). `usb_full_speed_mode.sh` toggles `dwc2.fs_ddma`; take its effect on interrupt load and its trade-offs from `docs/dwc2-usb-irq.md`, and note that document's open items. `cpu_isolation.sh` works live or through `isolcpus=`; explain why CPU1 from `docs/cpu-isolation.md` "Why CPU1". `security.sh` writes `/media/fat/linux/security.conf`; a missing key or file means stock (see the security page). pages.title: Build System
pages.purpose: Explain how the image is built: a plain Buildroot br2-external driven by a thin wrapper Makefile that fetches the pinned Buildroot release, verifies it against upstream's GPG-signed manifest, and forwards every goal to Buildroot with BR2_EXTERNAL and O= set. Give the commands to build each board and the SD card, the wrapper's own targets, the output files, host requirements and the uutils install shim, and the traps (no -j, re-run the defconfig after a pin move, keep defconfigs canonical).

page_notes.content:
Sources: `Makefile` (its header and every target), README "Building it yourself", `scripts/fetch-buildroot.sh`, `scripts/hostshim.sh`, ADR 0030 (`docs/decisions/0030-makefile-toward-vanilla-buildroot.md`), ADR 0001 (`docs/decisions/0001-toolchain.md`), `docs/reference-materials.md`, `external.desc`, `external.mk`.

Facts to get right. The wrapper adds only the Buildroot fetch-and-verify, the `hostshim` step, `de25`, `sdcard`, `buildroot-unpack`, `buildroot-verify`, `buildroot-showsig`, and Buildroot-meaning `clean`/`distclean` across output trees. Every other goal is forwarded by the `%:` catch-all. `O` defaults to `output/`; the DE25 builds in `output-de25/` (`make de25`). `dl/` is a shared download cache that survives `distclean`. `BUILDROOT_SHA256` is transcribed from the GPG-clearsigned release manifest by `scripts/hash-sync-buildroot.sh`, never from a downloaded tarball; the Makefile asks that both pin lines keep their exact shape because other scripts and `renovate.json` parse them.

`external.mk` includes every package `.mk` and carries a few build-wide adjustments: dhcpcd hooks, the coreutils/util-linux `kill` fix that errors out if Buildroot's coreutils.mk changes, the `-mtune=cortex-a9` kernel flag, and two U-Boot post-build audits (the DE25 QSPI-write audit and the DE10 resolved-config audit). Describe each from its comments.

`make` produces `output/images/linux.img`, `zImage_dtb`, `zImage_dtb-rt` and `mister-initramfs.cpio` (README). Give the README's target table and its "things that will bite you" list. Sources: `configs/mister_de10nano_defconfig` and `configs/mister_de25nano_defconfig` (their header comments), the top-level `Config.in`, `package/mister-userspace/Config.in`, `package/mister-firmware/Config.in`, `package/mister-drivers/Config.in`, `docs/buildroot-config.md` (read its "Layout change, 2026-09-11 (ADR 0030 Phase D)" box first: section 2 to 4 lines now live in the defconfigs, section 5 in `mister-userspace`, section 6 in `mister_de25nano_defconfig`, section 12 in `mister-firmware`; sections 1, 7, 8 and 11 are historical), ADR 0030 section 5.7, `scripts/check-defconfigs.sh`.
